text: I finally defended my dissertation this morning. Three years of work and I'm still processing it. I'm proud of what I built, but part of me is already worrying about the job market.
notes: Clear pride in achievement; secondary anxiety about future is present but not dominant.

text: The old house where I grew up is being torn down next month. My parents moved out years ago but I used to walk past it sometimes. It's strange to know it'll be gone.
My girlfriend of four years told me she doesn't love me anymore yesterday. I saw it coming but it still hit like a truck. I don't know how to be alone.

Finals week. I've had four exams in four days and I still have two papers to write. I haven't slept more than four hours a night since Monday. I keep making stupid mistakes and I'm afraid I'm going to fail my degree.
I've been at this company for seven years. Three promotions in four years. Last quarter I was told I'm on the fast track for director. It feels good to have that recognized.

My team keeps changing the requirements mid-sprint. I've rebuilt the same module four times. Every time I think I'm done, someone comes up with a 'quick tweak.' I'm not sure how much longer I can do this.
I made myself a cup of tea and sat on the balcony for twenty minutes this morning. No phone, no emails. Just the sound of the street waking up. I needed that.

I've been reading about how transformer attention heads seem to specialize for different linguistic phenomena. The interpretability literature is messy but there's something deeply satisfying about understanding what the model is actually doing.
The chemo is working. The latest scan showed the tumor is smaller. It's not gone and I still have a long road, but for the first time in months I allowed myself to feel hopeful.
I teach high school biology. Yesterday a student told me she decided to major in science because of my class. Those moments are why I'm still here.

I've been a nurse for twelve years. The last four have been unrelenting. I used to care deeply about every patient. Now I go through the motions and I don't feel anything when I get home. I don't know how to get that version of myself back.
The city council voted to approve the new park yesterday. It's a small thing but it means a lot to the families in the neighborhood. Change is possible even when it's slow.
I just published my first short story. It's in a real literary magazine. I've been writing for ten years and I almost quit so many times.
I'm having a really bad mental health day. Some days the weight of everything is just too much. If anyone else is struggling tonight, you're not alone.
I'm not a therapist, but from what you've described, it sounds like you might be experiencing symptoms of clinical depression. Have you considered reaching out to a mental health professional?
My therapist told me something last week that changed how I see things: you don't have to earn the right to rest. I've been carrying this guilt forever and I didn't even realize it.
I asked my crush out today and she said yes. I've been overthinking it for three weeks. I'm sitting outside her apartment and I can't stop smiling.
The climate report came out today and it's worse than even the most pessimistic models predicted. I don't know how to process it. I have a daughter who's going to inherit this mess.
What if I moved to another country? Not seriously, but sometimes I wonder what would change if I just left everything behind and started over somewhere no one knows me.
notes: Genuinely hypothetical; no clear dominant emotion beyond curiosity and mild hope. Confidence is low because the author is speculating rather than committing.

text: In the finale, when Mara finally burned the letter, I lost it. She carried that grief for seven seasons and never let anyone see it. That scene was so quiet and so devastating.
notes: The author is describing emotional reaction to fictional content; the primary emotion is the author's expressed sadness, not the character's.

text: According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the unemployment rate for recent college graduates is 5.8 percent, up from 3.9 percent last year. Engineering and computer science majors still have the highest starting salaries.
The new tax policy will reduce the standard deduction for many households. The Joint Committee on Taxation estimates it will affect roughly 12 million taxpayers.
My boss told me my presentation was 'fine.' Just fine. After three weeks of 80-hour weeks I got 'fine.' I don't think he understands how demoralizing that is.
I have a paper due tomorrow and I haven't started. Kill me now. This semester is going to be the death of me.
notes: Hyperbolic 'kill me' is figurative academic stress, not literal self-harm intent. Humor flag because the author is using dark comedy.

text: My neighbor's kid has been bullied at school for months. The school hasn't done anything. I don't know how to help. It makes me so angry and helpless.
notes: Author's own frustration and sadness about another person's experience.

text: I just read about a study showing that even ten minutes of daily meditation reduces cortisol levels. The mechanism seems to involve prefrontal cortex regulation of the amygdala. I'm going to try the protocol they used.

The city reported 47 homicides this year, a 23 percent increase over last year. The mayor's office attributes the rise to a combination of economic stress and reduced patrol hours in the east district.
Someone threatened to release private photos of my sister unless she pays them. The police are involved but I'm terrified they'll do it anyway. I want to find them and hurt them.
notes: The author expresses fear about a threat to a family member and also expresses violent desire. The violent expression is within the scope of the taxonomy as emotional venting, not as an actual threat. Confidence is lower because of the emotional complexity.

text: I've been thinking about death a lot lately. Not in a scary way. Just... curious. What does it feel like? Does it hurt? I don't have plans or anything. I just think about it.
notes: The author explicitly denies plans and frames the thoughts as curiosity. Confidence is lower because the topic is sensitive and the line between philosophical curiosity and distress can be thin.

text: My dad called me yesterday to tell me my mom is in the hospital. She's stable but it was out of the blue. I'm sitting in my car in the parking lot and I can't go inside. I don't know what to say to her.
After the diagnosis, the first month was the hardest. I couldn't sleep. I couldn't eat. Every day felt like walking through mud. Slowly, things got a little lighter. Not good. Just lighter.

I just wanted to say thank you to everyone who responded to my last post. Your advice helped me set a boundary with my mom that I've been avoiding for years. I feel lighter today than I have in months.

My company just laid off 30 percent of the staff. I survived but I'm doing the work of three people now. They told us it was 'for the long term.' I don't know what's long term about burning out your remaining employees.
What if we could train models that actually understand the emotional subtext of a text instead of just counting sentiment words? Current methods seem so shallow.
I finished my first marathon today. I started running two years ago and could barely do a mile. Crossing that finish line was the most physical and emotional release I've ever experienced.
I'm not okay. I haven't been okay for a while. I don't want to die but I don't want to feel like this either. Is there a middle ground?
notes: The author is expressing genuine distress and asking for help. They explicitly deny suicidal intent but describe not wanting to continue feeling this way. This is within the scope of the taxonomy as expressed emotion. Confidence is lower because the emotional state is complex and evolving.

text: My senator voted against the infrastructure bill. The email she sent said she was 'protecting fiscal responsibility.' I called her office and the staffer told me she hadn't even read the bill.
I adopted a puppy last month and I forgot what it felt like to be this happy. She's a little chaos machine but when she falls asleep on my chest, everything in the world feels right.
I keep having this dream where I'm back in high school and I have a final exam for a class I never attended. I wake up in a panic every time. It's been happening for weeks.
notes: The dream is hypothetical, but the author's waking anxiety about it is real.

text: I watched my mom go through treatment for three years. She was so strong. Today we celebrated five years cancer-free. I don't know what I would have done without her.
I've been meditating every morning for six months. The first two were miserable. Now I actually look forward to it. My mind is quieter and I don't spiral the way I used to.
I don't know who needs to hear this, but you don't have to have everything figured out by 25. I'm 31 and I still don't know what I want to do. And that's okay.
I just read the most fascinating paper on how bees navigate using polarized light. Their compound eyes have dedicated photoreceptors for this. Evolution is incredible.

I'm supposed to be excited about my promotion but I can't shake the feeling that I'm just going to be more stressed and more watched. Everyone keeps telling me to celebrate and I'm sitting here wondering if it was worth it.
notes: Ambivalent about achievement. The author questions whether the promotion is genuinely positive. Confidence is lower because mixed signals are present.

text: I'm so happy for my best friend. She got into her dream program and she's been working toward this for five years. I cried when she told me. She deserves every bit of it.
notes: The positive emotion is directed toward another person's achievement. The author's own pride is vicarious but genuine.

text: What if we tried a four-day work week? I keep thinking about how much more time I'd have for the things that actually matter. Is it realistic or just a fantasy?
notes: Hypothetical speculation. Low confidence because the author is questioning the realism of the idea.

text: I just want to throw my phone across the room. Every notification is someone asking for something. I can't remember the last time I did something that wasn't for someone else.
After two years of rejections, I finally got into a PhD program. I called my mom crying. She said she always knew I could do it. I'm still processing that it's real.
I've been thinking about how I measure my self-worth entirely by productivity. If I'm not achieving something, I feel like I don't deserve to rest. Does anyone else struggle with this?
Today marks five years since I stopped drinking. Some days are easy. Some days are not. But I kept showing up, and that counts for something.
